summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, diastolic dysfunction, and obstructive sleep apnea was admitted for chest pain radiating to the left arm, shortness of breath, and nausea. The pain was atypical and reproducible on chest wall palpation. Initial troponin was normal, second was mildly elevated at 0.04, but trended down to 0.01, in the setting of acute kidney injury likely due to reduced oral intake. EKG showed new right bundle branch block without ST changes. CT angiography ruled out pulmonary embolism. Stress test and echocardiogram showed no ischemia or wall motion abnormalities, with preserved ejection fraction of 57%. The chest pain responded to a GI cocktail and was attributed to gastroesophageal reflux. Her kidney function improved with hydration. Blood pressure was well-controlled inpatient, and labetalol was reduced to improve tolerance. She was discharged home on adjusted medications, including Maalox for symptom relief, with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider.
